storyMap.sidebar.aside.title: About this story map
storyMap.sidebar.aside.body: Exposure shows who could be affected in a modelled river flood, not who will be affected or who needs help. Example: Myanmar.
storyMap.header.description: It estimates how many children under 5 live in areas that could be flooded with more than 30 cm of water during a river flood with a 2% chance of happening in any given year. Exposure is one of three parts of risk, next to vulnerability and lack of coping capacity.

storyMap.sections.sec-flood.dataset.sour: JRC Global River Flood Hazard Maps
storyMap.sections.sec-flood.note.body:
The maps show **river floods only**: rivers overflowing their banks. Flash floods from heavy local rain, coastal floods and storm surge are not included.

Bigger, rarer floods reach further. The dashboard has indicators for all four scenarios.
storyMap.sections.sec-depth.title: Apply the flood-depth threshold
storyMap.sections.sec-depth.note.body:
Only places where the water is **deeper than 30 cm** count as exposed. HeiGIT chose this value because at that depth, water can knock people off their feet, stop vehicles and enter the ground floor of most homes.

The threshold is fixed: it was set when the indicators were calculated and can't be changed in the dashboard. The slider only illustrates it. Change the water depth to see when a place counts.
storyMap.sections.sec-depth.subtitle: Not every wet place is dangerous. A depth threshold splits the flooded area into two parts: places that are considered in the indicator, and places that are left out.
storyMap.sections.sec-who.title: Overlay people or facilities
storyMap.sections.sec-who.subtitle: Choose a group, then a flood scenario.
storyMap.sections.sec-who.note.body:
We lay a population map over the flood map. Everyone living in a flooded grid cell (about 100 × 100 m) counts as exposed.

The population maps are projections for **2030** (WorldPop). “Facilities” are schools, hospitals and health centres from OpenStreetMap.
storyMap.sections.sec-count.title: Aggregate to districts
storyMap.sections.sec-count.subtitle: 1-in-50-year river flood. Choose what to count.
storyMap.sections.sec-count.control.opti:
We add up all exposed children in the grid cells inside each district (see below). That gives one number per district: the value you see in the dashboard.

In Myanmar, about **980,000 children under 5** would be exposed in this scenario, roughly **1 in 4**.
We count the flooded facilities in each district. In Myanmar, about **1,040 facilities** would be in the water in this scenario.

storyMap.sections.sec-score.title: From count to colour
storyMap.sections.sec-score.note.body:
**Score:** each district gets a value from **0 to 1** within the country: 0 for the lowest district, 1 for the highest. The dashboard averages these scores over all active indicators, using your weights.

**Colour:** the districts are split into four equal groups (quartiles), so each colour always holds a quarter of them. That's why colours rank districts **within one country** and can't be compared between countries.
storyMap.sections.sec-score.subtitle: The dashboard doesn't map raw counts. It turns them into scores, and the scores into four colours.
storyMap.sections.sec-decoder.title: Decode any flood exposure indicator
storyMap.sections.sec-decoder.subtitle: Every flood exposure indicator in the dashboard follows the same pattern.
footer.callouts.positive.title: What this indicator tells us
footer.callouts.positive.items:
- where many people could be in harm's way in a given flood scenario
- which districts to look at first, compared with others in the same country
- how the picture changes for different groups and flood sizes
footer.callouts.warning.title: What this indicator does not tell us
footer.callouts.warning.items:
- whether or when a flood will happen; it is not a forecast
- how many people will be harmed or need help
- the effect of local protection, building quality or early warning
- flash floods from heavy local rain, coastal floods or storm surge; the maps cover river floods only
- anything precise about a single village: results are district totals from models
